1	# Customer-Side Features — Research Report
2	
3	_Compiled 2026-07-08. Scope: the CUSTOMER's side of a residential-cleaning business — public quote requests, online booking, quote acceptance + card capture, client portal (visits/invoices/proof-of-work), payments, and review collection. Grounds the customer-facing product we are adding to cleaner_crm (which today has only owner + cleaner surfaces). Sources cited inline; full list in §6._
4	
5	> **Framing.** The persisted corpus ([cleaner-pain-points.md](./cleaner-pain-points.md), [jobber.md](./jobber.md), [housecall-pro.md](./housecall-pro.md), [maidily-and-cleaning-specific.md](./maidily-and-cleaning-specific.md)) captures the OWNER/cleaner pains. This report is the mirror: what the person paying for cleaning experiences, and how incumbent customer surfaces behave. The single biggest cross-cutting finding: **the residential-cleaning category has bifurcated into "request-a-quote" FSM tools (Jobber, Housecall Pro) and "instant-quote" booking-first tools (BookingKoala, Launch27, ZenMaid) — and the instant-quote form is now the residential standard that converts.**
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. What customers want (evidence-backed)
10	
11	**Trust is the #1 gate, not cleaning quality.** A cited HomeAdvisor survey found **73% of people who had a negative cleaning experience blamed trust issues, not the cleaning itself** ([CleanSpace via search](https://cleanspace.com/resources/resources/how-to-choose-a-cleaning-service-you-can-trust-a-first-timers-guide)). You are inviting a stranger into your home with keys/codes — so the product must surface trust signals before it asks for a booking.
12	
13	Concrete trust signals customers screen for ([Merry Maids](https://merrymaids.com/blog/8-things-look-when-hiring-cleaning-service-company), [Rain City Maids](https://www.raincitymaids.com/10-signs-of-a-trustworthy-cleaning-company/), [Katie Cleans](https://katiecleans.com/questions-to-ask-a-cleaning-service/)):
14	- **Bonded, insured, background-checked cleaners** — described as "non-negotiable"; a service that can't confirm this on the spot loses the customer.
15	- **Named, photo-identified cleaner** — Jobber's Client Hub shows "photos of the team members assigned to the work" precisely because customers want to know who is coming ([Jobber Client Hub](https://www.getjobber.com/features/client-hub/)).
16	- **A satisfaction/re-clean guarantee** — reduces the perceived risk of a one-time trial.
17	- **Specific reviews, not star counts** — customers look for detail ("cleaned behind the stove, wiped inside the microwave without being asked") over aggregate ratings ([Aloha Maids](https://alohamaids.com/cleaning-service-reviews-what-they-tell-you-and-what-they-dont/)).
18	
19	**Transparent, upfront pricing wins; "bait-and-switch" pricing is a top complaint.** Customers want to "know what you're paying before booking"; the quoted rate shifting after the visit is one of the most common grievances ([CleanSpace](https://cleanspace.com/resources/resources/how-to-choose-a-cleaning-service-you-can-trust-a-first-timers-guide), [Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices)). This is the demand-side mirror of the owner-side "underpricing / walk-the-property" pain in [cleaner-pain-points.md §1.4](./cleaner-pain-points.md).
20	
21	**Instant pricing beats "request a quote" friction.** Booking can "take just a few seconds" and customers value booking directly without delay ([search synthesis](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices)). On time-pressured jobs (move-out), "the client is racing a handover deadline and hiring whoever answers first"; carrying pricing through quote→booking→payment "help[s] you win the job instead of trading texts about it" ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)). Listing add-ons in the form (vs. explaining them on every call) captures upsell revenue and reduces abandonment.
22	
23	**Self-service reschedule/cancel — within a fair policy.** Customers expect to change appointments online. Industry norm: **24-hour (some 48-hour) notice**, with cancellation fees of **10–15% or a flat $30–$50**, up to 50% inside 24h / 100% same-day ([Taskbird](https://www.taskbird.com/blog/residential-cleaning/cleaning-service-cancellation-policy), [Jobber](https://www.getjobber.com/academy/cleaning/cleaning-service-cancellation-policy/)). Best practice is to capture policy agreement at booking (checkbox / typed-name signature). This is the two-sided fix for the cancellation-churn pain that idles crews ([cleaner-pain-points.md §1.1](./cleaner-pain-points.md)).
24	
25	**Tipping expectations are rising and going digital.** Standard tip is **15–20%** ($10–$20/visit); one-time/deep cleans **20–30%**. For recurring clients, per-visit tipping is NOT expected — the norm is a **holiday "Rule of One" bonus = one cleaning's cost**. Over 50% of tips are now digital (Venmo/Zelle/CashApp), and **"subscription tipping" (a flat monthly gratuity added to the digital payment) is a rising 2026 trend** ([Care.com](https://www.care.com/c/how-much-to-tip-a-house-cleaner/), [Arion Clean](https://arionclean.com/house-cleaning-prices/how-much-tip-for-house-cleaner-whats-fair-generous-and-expected-in-2025/), [TIDY](https://www.tidy.com/blog/to-tip-or-not-to-tip-the-guide-to-tipping-your-house-cleaner)). Owner-side, tips are poorly tracked in incumbents (Jobber has no native tip tracking — [jobber.md §4](./jobber.md)), so an in-portal tip prompt is both a customer convenience and a cleaner-retention lever.
26	
27	**Communication that reaches them.** Customers' top grievances are "missed appointments, lack of communication" ([cleaner-pain-points.md §1.6](./cleaner-pain-points.md)). They want confirmations, "on-my-way" texts, and one authoritative place for appointment details — not phone tag.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## 2. Incumbent customer surfaces (Jobber / HCP / booking-first tools)
32	
33	### Jobber — Client Hub (its genuine differentiator)
34	A 24/7 self-serve portal. From the customer's side they can ([Jobber Client Hub](https://www.getjobber.com/features/client-hub/), [Help Center](https://help.getjobber.com/hc/en-us/articles/360046586294-A-Guide-for-Your-Clients-How-to-Navigate-Client-Hub)):
35	- **Approve quotes or request changes online** (free-text box to describe desired changes); provider is notified the moment it's approved and the quote **auto-converts to a scheduled job** ([Jobber search result](https://help.getjobber.com/hc/en-us/articles/115009611207-Quote-Deposits-and-Jobber-Payments)).
36	- **Approve + pay a required deposit in ONE step** — "Approve & Pay"; deposit collected simultaneously with booking confirmation.
37	- **View past & upcoming appointments**, including **photos of the assigned team members** (trust signal).
38	- **Pay invoices/deposits online** and **add a tip** at payment.
39	- **Request new work** and **refer via social share links**.
40	- Gap: the underlying quoting is request-based — a human still builds the quote. Jobber does **not** offer true instant self-quoting with automated pricing ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).
41	
42	### Housecall Pro — Online Booking + Review Automation
43	- **Online booking widget** embeddable on any site and bookable "directly from Google" — customer self-schedules; both sides get text + email confirmation ([HCP Online Booking](https://help.housecallpro.com/en/articles/7034474-online-booking-overview)). Customizable intake flow collects info upfront.
44	- **Customer portal**: view services, approve estimates, pay invoices, book appointments ([housecall-pro.md §2](./housecall-pro.md)).
45	- **Review automation is HCP's single most-praised cleaning feature** — see §4. Reported **2–3x (some say 3–5x) more Google reviews** ([housecall-pro.md §4](./housecall-pro.md)).
46	- **Payments**: cards/ACH/wallets, cards-on-file auto-charge for recurring visits, same-day deposits (Instapay), Klarna consumer financing ([housecall-pro.md §2](./housecall-pro.md)).
47	- Gap: like Jobber, booking is request/flat-rate oriented, **not** per-bedroom instant quoting ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).
48	
49	### Booking-first tools (the instant-quote standard)
50	- **BookingKoala** (~$27/mo start): "bedroom-bathroom pricing calculators out of the box," white-label booking forms, coupons, gift cards, customer referral portal; strong for franchise/multi-territory ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-online-booking-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).
51	- **Launch27 / Automaid**: embeddable widget with **bedroom-bathroom-square-foot pricing logic** + cleaner commission splits; higher base price (~$299/mo Plus).
52	- **ZenMaid**: embeddable forms with bedroom-bathroom logic + recurring automation; pricing by home size, rooms, service type.
53	- **QuoteIQ InstaQuote**: "configure pricing rules once, and the system quotes every customer automatically, 24/7," real-time total as the customer builds the quote — no callback required.
54	
55	**Takeaway:** the FSM incumbents own the portal/payments/reviews surface but leave a hole on **instant self-serve pricing**; the booking-first tools own instant pricing but are thinner on the deep client portal, proof-of-work, and mature payments. A cleaner-native product can do both.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 3. Standard instant-quote calculator anatomy
60	
61	This is the residential-cleaning conversion workhorse. Composite of Thumbtack pricing data, BookingKoala/Launch27/ZenMaid/QuoteIQ forms ([Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices), [QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).
62	
63	**Fields the customer selects (price recomputes live on each change):**
64	1. **Service type** — Standard/Regular, Deep, Move-in/Move-out, Post-construction, Vacation-rental/STR turnover. (Sets the base rate.)
65	2. **Bedrooms** (typ. studio→5+) and **Bathrooms** (typ. 1→4+) — the primary size drivers.
66	3. **Square footage** — used instead of or alongside bedroom/bath (some price purely per sq-ft).
67	4. **Frequency** — One-time / Weekly / Bi-weekly (every 2 wks) / Monthly — applies the recurring discount.
68	5. **Add-ons / extras** — inside fridge, inside oven, interior windows, laundry/wash-and-fold, baseboards, inside cabinets, dishes, pet-hair surcharge. Each a flat add or per-unit.
69	6. **Date/time** preference, then **contact details**, then **address**, then **card capture**.
70	
71	**Pricing math (typical model):** `base rate (by service type) → + per-bedroom and per-bathroom increments (or sq-ft × rate) → + Σ add-ons → × frequency discount multiplier → optional coupon/gift card → tax`. Per-sq-ft benchmark: **~$0.05/sqft standard, ~$0.10/sqft deep** ([Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices)).
72	
73	**Real market anchors (national, [Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices)):**
74	- One-time standard visit: **$174–$256** (national avg); hourly **$40–$55/hr**.
75	- By bedrooms: 1BR $133–$174 · 2BR $136–$217 · 3BR $166–$250 · 4BR $191–$286.
76	- By bathrooms: 1BA $139–$189 · 2BA $174–$235 · 3BA $203–$274.
77	- By service: Standard $146–$202 · Deep $190–$265 · Move-out $200–$286 · STR $179–$257 · Post-construction $203–$285.
78	- Add-ons (delta to total): laundry $176–$261 · fridge $187–$268 · oven $195–$273 · interior windows $196–$274.
79	
80	**Frequency discount (the recurring hook):** one-time $174–$256 → every-2-weeks $160–$220 → monthly $162–$228. The discount converts one-time buyers into recurring subscription revenue — the core of residential cleaning economics. Configure as a % off base (e.g. weekly −20%, bi-weekly −15%, monthly −10%).
81	
82	**Design rules that reduce abandonment:** show a **running total** as they build; expose **add-ons in the form** so customers self-select extras (captures upsell, avoids "some duties cost extra" disputes — [cleaner-pain-points.md §2.1](./cleaner-pain-points.md)); **no forced phone call** to see price; carry the same number straight through to booking + card capture. Track **quote acceptance / close rate — aim 65–75%** and adjust prices 5–10% at a time ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).
83	
84	---
85	
86	## 4. Review collection mechanics that work
87	
88	HCP's model is the proven template (reported **2–3x** more Google reviews with zero manual effort — the reason cleaners tolerate HCP's price, [housecall-pro.md §4](./housecall-pro.md)). Mechanics ([HCP Reviews Overview](https://help.housecallpro.com/en/articles/2637765-reviews-overview)):
89	
90	- **Trigger:** fires automatically on **job "Finish"** (default) or on **job paid** (configurable) — no manual send.
91	- **Channel:** sends via **both SMS and email** with previews of each.
92	- **Smart routing:** by default routes **Gmail-address customers → Google** (where the review counts most for local search), then splits the rest between Facebook and the business website. Owner can override to 100% one platform.
93	- **No review gating/filtering:** every customer gets the request; negative reviews are NOT intercepted (some competitors gate low ratings to a private feedback form — legally gray under FTC rules, so HCP's open model is the safer default).
94	- **Follow-ups:** customizable SMS/email reminders for non-responders (HCP help docs are vague on exact cadence; ~24h delayed first ask + follow-ups is the cited best practice — [housecall-pro.md §2](./housecall-pro.md)).
95	- **Owner tooling:** manage/respond to reviews in one place; HCP layers **postcard reactivation** marketing on top ([housecall-pro.md](./housecall-pro.md)).
96	
97	**What "works" distilled:** automatic trigger tied to job completion + delayed ask (~24h) + dual SMS/email + direct deep-link to the Google review page + follow-up nudges + smart routing to Google. This directly attacks the owner pain that review generation is unsystematic ([cleaner-pain-points.md §1.9](./cleaner-pain-points.md)).
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 5. Gaps / opportunities for a cleaner-specific product
102	
103	1. **Own BOTH instant-quote AND the deep client portal.** Jobber/HCP have the portal + payments + reviews but only request-based quoting; BookingKoala/Launch27 have instant quoting but thinner portals/payments/proof-of-work. **No incumbent does both well.** A cleaner-native instant-quote calculator (§3) feeding a Jobber-grade Client Hub is the wedge.
104	2. **Proof-of-work in the customer portal — not just STR.** Photo-proof, room-by-room checklists, and before/after photos are standard in STR tools (Turno/Properly) but "largely absent from residential" client-facing surfaces ([cleaner-pain-points.md §5.3](./cleaner-pain-points.md)). Surfacing per-visit completed checklists + photos in the client portal resolves "missed spots" disputes and **defends against chargebacks** — a documented payment pain ([cleaner-pain-points.md §1.8](./cleaner-pain-points.md)).
105	3. **Trust signals as first-class product surface.** Bonded/insured/background-checked badges, named + photo-identified assigned cleaner, and a satisfaction guarantee shown BEFORE booking — directly answers the 73%-trust-gate finding. Incumbents bury this; make it the public quote/booking page's spine.
106	4. **One-step quote-accept + card capture + deposit** (Jobber's best flow) combined with **recurring subscription setup** — capture card on file at acceptance so recurring visits auto-charge (kills the "couldn't process payment" trust-loss pain — [cleaner-pain-points.md §1.8](./cleaner-pain-points.md)).
107	5. **Native tipping built for recurring reality.** In-portal tip prompt at payment (15–20% presets), a **holiday "Rule of One" bonus** nudge in December, and **subscription tipping** (flat monthly gratuity) — none of which incumbents model well (Jobber can't track tips natively). Feeds cleaner retention.
108	6. **Self-service reschedule/cancel that enforces the policy.** Customer-facing reschedule/cancel with the 24–48h window + fee logic and policy-agreement capture at booking — two-sided relief for cancellation churn.
109	7. **Deliverable review automation on a trusted domain.** Copy HCP's trigger→delay→dual-channel→Google-routing model, but avoid Jobber's deliverability failure (generic `jobbermail.com` — "60% of estimates went unviewed," [jobber.md §4](./jobber.md)). Reliable SMS/email delivery of confirmations, reminders, and review asks is itself a differentiator.
110	8. **Transparent, no-surprise pricing as brand promise.** Since bait-and-switch is a top complaint, make "the price you see is the price you pay" a product guarantee — the instant quote number IS the invoice number.

# Customer-Side Features — Research Report

_Compiled 2026-07-08. Scope: the CUSTOMER's side of a residential-cleaning business — public quote requests, online booking, quote acceptance + card capture, client portal (visits/invoices/proof-of-work), payments, and review collection. Grounds the customer-facing product we are adding to cleaner_crm (which today has only owner + cleaner surfaces). Sources cited inline; full list in §6._

> **Framing.** The persisted corpus ([cleaner-pain-points.md](./cleaner-pain-points.md), [jobber.md](./jobber.md), [housecall-pro.md](./housecall-pro.md), [maidily-and-cleaning-specific.md](./maidily-and-cleaning-specific.md)) captures the OWNER/cleaner pains. This report is the mirror: what the person paying for cleaning experiences, and how incumbent customer surfaces behave. The single biggest cross-cutting finding: **the residential-cleaning category has bifurcated into "request-a-quote" FSM tools (Jobber, Housecall Pro) and "instant-quote" booking-first tools (BookingKoala, Launch27, ZenMaid) — and the instant-quote form is now the residential standard that converts.**

---

## 1. What customers want (evidence-backed)

**Trust is the #1 gate, not cleaning quality.** A cited HomeAdvisor survey found **73% of people who had a negative cleaning experience blamed trust issues, not the cleaning itself** ([CleanSpace via search](https://cleanspace.com/resources/resources/how-to-choose-a-cleaning-service-you-can-trust-a-first-timers-guide)). You are inviting a stranger into your home with keys/codes — so the product must surface trust signals before it asks for a booking.

Concrete trust signals customers screen for ([Merry Maids](https://merrymaids.com/blog/8-things-look-when-hiring-cleaning-service-company), [Rain City Maids](https://www.raincitymaids.com/10-signs-of-a-trustworthy-cleaning-company/), [Katie Cleans](https://katiecleans.com/questions-to-ask-a-cleaning-service/)):
- **Bonded, insured, background-checked cleaners** — described as "non-negotiable"; a service that can't confirm this on the spot loses the customer.
- **Named, photo-identified cleaner** — Jobber's Client Hub shows "photos of the team members assigned to the work" precisely because customers want to know who is coming ([Jobber Client Hub](https://www.getjobber.com/features/client-hub/)).
- **A satisfaction/re-clean guarantee** — reduces the perceived risk of a one-time trial.
- **Specific reviews, not star counts** — customers look for detail ("cleaned behind the stove, wiped inside the microwave without being asked") over aggregate ratings ([Aloha Maids](https://alohamaids.com/cleaning-service-reviews-what-they-tell-you-and-what-they-dont/)).

**Transparent, upfront pricing wins; "bait-and-switch" pricing is a top complaint.** Customers want to "know what you're paying before booking"; the quoted rate shifting after the visit is one of the most common grievances ([CleanSpace](https://cleanspace.com/resources/resources/how-to-choose-a-cleaning-service-you-can-trust-a-first-timers-guide), [Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices)). This is the demand-side mirror of the owner-side "underpricing / walk-the-property" pain in [cleaner-pain-points.md §1.4](./cleaner-pain-points.md).

**Instant pricing beats "request a quote" friction.** Booking can "take just a few seconds" and customers value booking directly without delay ([search synthesis](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices)). On time-pressured jobs (move-out), "the client is racing a handover deadline and hiring whoever answers first"; carrying pricing through quote→booking→payment "help[s] you win the job instead of trading texts about it" ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)). Listing add-ons in the form (vs. explaining them on every call) captures upsell revenue and reduces abandonment.

**Self-service reschedule/cancel — within a fair policy.** Customers expect to change appointments online. Industry norm: **24-hour (some 48-hour) notice**, with cancellation fees of **10–15% or a flat $30–$50**, up to 50% inside 24h / 100% same-day ([Taskbird](https://www.taskbird.com/blog/residential-cleaning/cleaning-service-cancellation-policy), [Jobber](https://www.getjobber.com/academy/cleaning/cleaning-service-cancellation-policy/)). Best practice is to capture policy agreement at booking (checkbox / typed-name signature). This is the two-sided fix for the cancellation-churn pain that idles crews ([cleaner-pain-points.md §1.1](./cleaner-pain-points.md)).

**Tipping expectations are rising and going digital.** Standard tip is **15–20%** ($10–$20/visit); one-time/deep cleans **20–30%**. For recurring clients, per-visit tipping is NOT expected — the norm is a **holiday "Rule of One" bonus = one cleaning's cost**. Over 50% of tips are now digital (Venmo/Zelle/CashApp), and **"subscription tipping" (a flat monthly gratuity added to the digital payment) is a rising 2026 trend** ([Care.com](https://www.care.com/c/how-much-to-tip-a-house-cleaner/), [Arion Clean](https://arionclean.com/house-cleaning-prices/how-much-tip-for-house-cleaner-whats-fair-generous-and-expected-in-2025/), [TIDY](https://www.tidy.com/blog/to-tip-or-not-to-tip-the-guide-to-tipping-your-house-cleaner)). Owner-side, tips are poorly tracked in incumbents (Jobber has no native tip tracking — [jobber.md §4](./jobber.md)), so an in-portal tip prompt is both a customer convenience and a cleaner-retention lever.

**Communication that reaches them.** Customers' top grievances are "missed appointments, lack of communication" ([cleaner-pain-points.md §1.6](./cleaner-pain-points.md)). They want confirmations, "on-my-way" texts, and one authoritative place for appointment details — not phone tag.

---

## 2. Incumbent customer surfaces (Jobber / HCP / booking-first tools)

### Jobber — Client Hub (its genuine differentiator)
A 24/7 self-serve portal. From the customer's side they can ([Jobber Client Hub](https://www.getjobber.com/features/client-hub/), [Help Center](https://help.getjobber.com/hc/en-us/articles/360046586294-A-Guide-for-Your-Clients-How-to-Navigate-Client-Hub)):
- **Approve quotes or request changes online** (free-text box to describe desired changes); provider is notified the moment it's approved and the quote **auto-converts to a scheduled job** ([Jobber search result](https://help.getjobber.com/hc/en-us/articles/115009611207-Quote-Deposits-and-Jobber-Payments)).
- **Approve + pay a required deposit in ONE step** — "Approve & Pay"; deposit collected simultaneously with booking confirmation.
- **View past & upcoming appointments**, including **photos of the assigned team members** (trust signal).
- **Pay invoices/deposits online** and **add a tip** at payment.
- **Request new work** and **refer via social share links**.
- Gap: the underlying quoting is request-based — a human still builds the quote. Jobber does **not** offer true instant self-quoting with automated pricing ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).

### Housecall Pro — Online Booking + Review Automation
- **Online booking widget** embeddable on any site and bookable "directly from Google" — customer self-schedules; both sides get text + email confirmation ([HCP Online Booking](https://help.housecallpro.com/en/articles/7034474-online-booking-overview)). Customizable intake flow collects info upfront.
- **Customer portal**: view services, approve estimates, pay invoices, book appointments ([housecall-pro.md §2](./housecall-pro.md)).
- **Review automation is HCP's single most-praised cleaning feature** — see §4. Reported **2–3x (some say 3–5x) more Google reviews** ([housecall-pro.md §4](./housecall-pro.md)).
- **Payments**: cards/ACH/wallets, cards-on-file auto-charge for recurring visits, same-day deposits (Instapay), Klarna consumer financing ([housecall-pro.md §2](./housecall-pro.md)).
- Gap: like Jobber, booking is request/flat-rate oriented, **not** per-bedroom instant quoting ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).

### Booking-first tools (the instant-quote standard)
- **BookingKoala** (~$27/mo start): "bedroom-bathroom pricing calculators out of the box," white-label booking forms, coupons, gift cards, customer referral portal; strong for franchise/multi-territory ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-online-booking-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).
- **Launch27 / Automaid**: embeddable widget with **bedroom-bathroom-square-foot pricing logic** + cleaner commission splits; higher base price (~$299/mo Plus).
- **ZenMaid**: embeddable forms with bedroom-bathroom logic + recurring automation; pricing by home size, rooms, service type.
- **QuoteIQ InstaQuote**: "configure pricing rules once, and the system quotes every customer automatically, 24/7," real-time total as the customer builds the quote — no callback required.

**Takeaway:** the FSM incumbents own the portal/payments/reviews surface but leave a hole on **instant self-serve pricing**; the booking-first tools own instant pricing but are thinner on the deep client portal, proof-of-work, and mature payments. A cleaner-native product can do both.

---

## 3. Standard instant-quote calculator anatomy

This is the residential-cleaning conversion workhorse. Composite of Thumbtack pricing data, BookingKoala/Launch27/ZenMaid/QuoteIQ forms ([Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices), [QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).

**Fields the customer selects (price recomputes live on each change):**
1. **Service type** — Standard/Regular, Deep, Move-in/Move-out, Post-construction, Vacation-rental/STR turnover. (Sets the base rate.)
2. **Bedrooms** (typ. studio→5+) and **Bathrooms** (typ. 1→4+) — the primary size drivers.
3. **Square footage** — used instead of or alongside bedroom/bath (some price purely per sq-ft).
4. **Frequency** — One-time / Weekly / Bi-weekly (every 2 wks) / Monthly — applies the recurring discount.
5. **Add-ons / extras** — inside fridge, inside oven, interior windows, laundry/wash-and-fold, baseboards, inside cabinets, dishes, pet-hair surcharge. Each a flat add or per-unit.
6. **Date/time** preference, then **contact details**, then **address**, then **card capture**.

**Pricing math (typical model):** `base rate (by service type) → + per-bedroom and per-bathroom increments (or sq-ft × rate) → + Σ add-ons → × frequency discount multiplier → optional coupon/gift card → tax`. Per-sq-ft benchmark: **~$0.05/sqft standard, ~$0.10/sqft deep** ([Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices)).

**Real market anchors (national, [Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/house-cleaning-prices)):**
- One-time standard visit: **$174–$256** (national avg); hourly **$40–$55/hr**.
- By bedrooms: 1BR $133–$174 · 2BR $136–$217 · 3BR $166–$250 · 4BR $191–$286.
- By bathrooms: 1BA $139–$189 · 2BA $174–$235 · 3BA $203–$274.
- By service: Standard $146–$202 · Deep $190–$265 · Move-out $200–$286 · STR $179–$257 · Post-construction $203–$285.
- Add-ons (delta to total): laundry $176–$261 · fridge $187–$268 · oven $195–$273 · interior windows $196–$274.

**Frequency discount (the recurring hook):** one-time $174–$256 → every-2-weeks $160–$220 → monthly $162–$228. The discount converts one-time buyers into recurring subscription revenue — the core of residential cleaning economics. Configure as a % off base (e.g. weekly −20%, bi-weekly −15%, monthly −10%).

**Design rules that reduce abandonment:** show a **running total** as they build; expose **add-ons in the form** so customers self-select extras (captures upsell, avoids "some duties cost extra" disputes — [cleaner-pain-points.md §2.1](./cleaner-pain-points.md)); **no forced phone call** to see price; carry the same number straight through to booking + card capture. Track **quote acceptance / close rate — aim 65–75%** and adjust prices 5–10% at a time ([QuoteIQ](https://myquoteiq.com/best-customer-self-quoting-software-cleaning-businesses-2026/)).

---

## 4. Review collection mechanics that work

HCP's model is the proven template (reported **2–3x** more Google reviews with zero manual effort — the reason cleaners tolerate HCP's price, [housecall-pro.md §4](./housecall-pro.md)). Mechanics ([HCP Reviews Overview](https://help.housecallpro.com/en/articles/2637765-reviews-overview)):

- **Trigger:** fires automatically on **job "Finish"** (default) or on **job paid** (configurable) — no manual send.
- **Channel:** sends via **both SMS and email** with previews of each.
- **Smart routing:** by default routes **Gmail-address customers → Google** (where the review counts most for local search), then splits the rest between Facebook and the business website. Owner can override to 100% one platform.
- **No review gating/filtering:** every customer gets the request; negative reviews are NOT intercepted (some competitors gate low ratings to a private feedback form — legally gray under FTC rules, so HCP's open model is the safer default).
- **Follow-ups:** customizable SMS/email reminders for non-responders (HCP help docs are vague on exact cadence; ~24h delayed first ask + follow-ups is the cited best practice — [housecall-pro.md §2](./housecall-pro.md)).
- **Owner tooling:** manage/respond to reviews in one place; HCP layers **postcard reactivation** marketing on top ([housecall-pro.md](./housecall-pro.md)).

**What "works" distilled:** automatic trigger tied to job completion + delayed ask (~24h) + dual SMS/email + direct deep-link to the Google review page + follow-up nudges + smart routing to Google. This directly attacks the owner pain that review generation is unsystematic ([cleaner-pain-points.md §1.9](./cleaner-pain-points.md)).

---

## 5. Gaps / opportunities for a cleaner-specific product

1. **Own BOTH instant-quote AND the deep client portal.** Jobber/HCP have the portal + payments + reviews but only request-based quoting; BookingKoala/Launch27 have instant quoting but thinner portals/payments/proof-of-work. **No incumbent does both well.** A cleaner-native instant-quote calculator (§3) feeding a Jobber-grade Client Hub is the wedge.
2. **Proof-of-work in the customer portal — not just STR.** Photo-proof, room-by-room checklists, and before/after photos are standard in STR tools (Turno/Properly) but "largely absent from residential" client-facing surfaces ([cleaner-pain-points.md §5.3](./cleaner-pain-points.md)). Surfacing per-visit completed checklists + photos in the client portal resolves "missed spots" disputes and **defends against chargebacks** — a documented payment pain ([cleaner-pain-points.md §1.8](./cleaner-pain-points.md)).
3. **Trust signals as first-class product surface.** Bonded/insured/background-checked badges, named + photo-identified assigned cleaner, and a satisfaction guarantee shown BEFORE booking — directly answers the 73%-trust-gate finding. Incumbents bury this; make it the public quote/booking page's spine.
4. **One-step quote-accept + card capture + deposit** (Jobber's best flow) combined with **recurring subscription setup** — capture card on file at acceptance so recurring visits auto-charge (kills the "couldn't process payment" trust-loss pain — [cleaner-pain-points.md §1.8](./cleaner-pain-points.md)).
5. **Native tipping built for recurring reality.** In-portal tip prompt at payment (15–20% presets), a **holiday "Rule of One" bonus** nudge in December, and **subscription tipping** (flat monthly gratuity) — none of which incumbents model well (Jobber can't track tips natively). Feeds cleaner retention.
6. **Self-service reschedule/cancel that enforces the policy.** Customer-facing reschedule/cancel with the 24–48h window + fee logic and policy-agreement capture at booking — two-sided relief for cancellation churn.
7. **Deliverable review automation on a trusted domain.** Copy HCP's trigger→delay→dual-channel→Google-routing model, but avoid Jobber's deliverability failure (generic `jobbermail.com` — "60% of estimates went unviewed," [jobber.md §4](./jobber.md)). Reliable SMS/email delivery of confirmations, reminders, and review asks is itself a differentiator.
8. **Transparent, no-surprise pricing as brand promise.** Since bait-and-switch is a top complaint, make "the price you see is the price you pay" a product guarantee — the instant quote number IS the invoice number.

---

Feature: Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  As a cleaning business owner, I want jobs to generate invoices on completion and collect payment via card-on-file or payment link, so that I get paid without chasing clients and disputes are backed by proof-of-work evidence. (Research: payment failures and chargebacks are acute owner pains — pain-points §1.8)
  Rule: Marking a job complete automatically generates an invoice for that job at its agreed price.
    Scenario: Completing a job generates its invoice
      Given a scheduled job has an agreed price of $150
      When the cleaner marks the job complete
      Then an invoice for $150 is generated for that job and appears in the owner's billing queue

  Rule: An invoice can be collected by charging the client's card-on-file or by sending the client a payment link.
    Scenario: Auto-charge the card on file
      Given a client has a valid card on file
      When the invoice is generated and the owner charges the card on file
      Then the card is charged for the invoice amount and the client receives a receipt

    Scenario: Client with no card on file pays via payment link
      Given a client has no card on file
      When the owner sends the invoice as a payment link and the client pays it online
      Then the invoice is collected and the client's card can be saved for next time

  Rule: Each invoice carries the completed job's proof-of-work — checklist and before/after photos — as evidence for billing disputes.
    Scenario: Invoice shows the job's proof-of-work
      Given a job was completed with a finished checklist and before/after photos
      When the invoice for that job is opened
      Then the completed checklist and photos are attached to the invoice as dispute evidence

  Rule: A declined or failed card charge leaves the invoice unpaid and alerts the owner to retry or send a payment link.
    Scenario: Card-on-file charge is declined
      Given an invoice is set to auto-charge the card on file
      When the payment provider declines the card
      Then the invoice remains unpaid and the owner is alerted to retry the charge or send a payment link

  Rule: An invoice is marked paid only after the payment provider confirms the charge succeeded.
    Scenario: Invoice marked paid on provider confirmation
      Given an invoice charge has been submitted to the payment provider
      When the provider confirms the charge succeeded
      Then the invoice is marked paid and the owner sees it settled in the billing queue
